manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the blackboard eraser and throw it into the trash bin.

Task description: The target is the long board eraser with a black wiping surface and gray-white base, on the table left of the bin and below the mouse. Pick it up with the right gripper and put it in the adjacent open bin lined with a black garbage bag.

Success criteria: The blackboard eraser has been picked up from the table and remains inside the trash bin after the gripper releases it. Merely holding it above the bin opening does not count.

## Execution tips

- Grip the middle sections of the eraser's long sides, opening slightly wider than its width. Contact the gray-white base sides with the pads while leaving fingertip clearance above the table, reducing slippage from gripping soft-surface corners.
- Before closing, use different views to confirm the fingers are on opposite sides of the eraser. During a slight lift, observe whether it leaves the table with the gripper. If it slips, restore table support before adjusting.
- When moving laterally into the bin, keep both the eraser’s lowest point and the gripper above the rim and raised bag opening, avoiding impact with the bin or catching the trash bag with a fingertip.
- Release with the entire eraser body inside the bin's inner rim and its fall path clear of the folded bag edge. Keep the drop short where possible to reduce bouncing or landing outside the bin.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill for this authorized real-robot episode strictly with the given parameters, following the returned manual and live observations.

I have read the returned manual and confirmed the eraser is left of the bin. Only the right arm is available. I am adjusting gripper orientation and approach position, then will align in small steps and verify grasp security.

The gripper is above the blackboard eraser, which remains flat on the table. Next I will reduce the movement size, align both fingers with the middle of its long sides, and maintain clearance from the table.

A pose adjustment reached the controller's joint limits. Using the returned measured position, I switched to a reachable diagonal downward grasp pose. I am now approaching the target and will descend in steps no greater than 1 cm, observing after each.

Both gripper fingers are aligned across the blackboard eraser's width, and it has not moved yet. I will continue lowering slightly, confirm the pads reach its sides before closing, then validate the grasp with a short lift.

The measured gripper opening after closure is about 56 mm. The eraser followed the gripper during a short lift, indicating initial stability. I will raise it further so both eraser and fingers clear the bin rim before moving sideways.

The blackboard eraser is clearly off the table, with no visible slipping. During the lift I will adjust the wrist pose to avoid joint limits while staying in the open area to the left of the trash bin.

The blackboard eraser remains securely grasped. The current lift height is not enough to confirm clearance above the folded bag opening, so I will raise it further outside the bin, then align with the opening from above.
The gripper is about 45 cm high and holds the blackboard eraser. I am moving laterally toward the trash bin, checking the rim and bag opening in both views.

The grip remained stable during lateral movement. The wrist view still does not show the center of the bin opening clearly, so I will first adjust to reveal the inner rim, then decide where to release.
The wrist view now shows the bin opening, but the eraser remains left of it. I will adjust inward in 1 cm steps to confirm the entire eraser's drop footprint lies within the inner rim.

The right and rear inner edges of the bin opening are now more visible, and the blackboard eraser has not been released. I am making small lateral moves while maintaining height, gradually bringing the drop point inside the bin.
Both views show the blackboard eraser above the bin opening, still with clearance from the bag mouth. I will make small position and height corrections, confirm the drop area, then release it.

The blackboard eraser is aligned over the inside of the bin opening, and the image shows no contact with the bag edge. I will release the gripper and observe whether it lands inside, bounces, or catches on the rim.

The eraser detached and fell below the bin rim, with no bounce-out or rim hanging observed. The trash bag and viewing angle obscure the bottom. I will end this episode; final success remains for the on-site operator to confirm.
